newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-IAAF TO INTRODUCE WORLD RECORD BONUSES - SOURCES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF TO INTRODUCE WORLD RECORD BONUSES - SOURCES.

text.p: Athletes setting world records at next year's Athens world championships could earn a $100,000 bonus, International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) sources said on Wednesday.
"We have a sponsor who will put up to $100,000 for world records," the sources said.
They added the IAAF council would make a formal decision next month at its Monaco headquarters whether to introduce prize money at both its indoor and outdoor world championships.

At last year's Gothenburg world championships Kenyan Moses Kiptanui deliberately slowed down in the 3,000 metres steeplechase final with the world record in sight. Shortly afterwards he broke the record in Zurich, earning a handsome bonus for his efforts.
The sources said the council had been due to make a decision on the venue of the 1999 world championships at its meeting on December 10-11 but had now decided to wait until next March.
Helsinki, New Delhi. Seville, Spain and Stanford, California are the candidate cities.
The IAAF arbitration panel will meet in Monaco this Sunday and Monday to consider the drug cases of Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco and Italian high jumper Antonella Bevilacqua respectively.
The pair were allowed to compete at the Atlanta Olympics despite failing drugs tests after the IAAF's legal advisors said the federation could be sued successfully in a civil court.
Bevilacqua tested positive twice last May for the stimulant ephedrine but an Italian panel ruled she had taken the drug by accident and did not impose the statutory three-month ban.
Capobianco tested positive for the steroid stanozolol, the drug used by Ben Johnson at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, at a meeting in the Dutch town of Hengelo in the same month.
He escaped a four-year ban when his national governing body Athletics Australia cleared him on the grounds that the testing procedures had been seriously flawed.
